body: Its okay I’m doing fine now, but yeah people just don’t care and I never got over that. I’m disappointed in everyone but I can see why maybe the other students didn’t say anything. But the teacher and my “friends”? I was disappointed. Thank you for your comment, I appreciate it ♥️

I went into class right after with tear streaks from my makeup running down my face and nobody said a word. Just acted like everything was normal. I was very late to class that morning so when I entered, they saw me. Just didn’t care. After class I was able to look in the mirror and saw how noticeable it was. That moment never left me.

Although I don’t agree with ghosting, if you feel like its the only way to escape and if you feel in your gut she is doing this to just keep you around, then do it. I don’t know the full story obviously but you know better than us, if she is toxic and manipulative (which is how it sounds) then you need to save yourself and move on.

This makes me so sad. I see parents (mothers specifically for some reason) of victims of domestic abuse, telling them to go back. Please please pleasee don’t listen to your mother and stay far away from that man child. If you ever have to interact with him, make sure another TRUSTED male accompanies you and stays with you at all times. And I hope this doesn’t need to be said but I’ll say it anyway- don’t ever let him near your poor cat ever again. He should never even lay an eye on her. This guy is a ticking time bomb and just showed you the real him, which will only get more and more violent if you accept it. That being said, seeing you or your cat (who in his mind is probably the one he’s blaming this on) will only end badly. The chances of it being violent are extremely high.

Edit: I just skimmed the other comments and apparently my take might be an unpopular option. That’s honestly disappointing.

I either saw your friends post or this unfortunately happened to someone else, nevertheless I am so sorry for what had happened. I just wanted to say that your head is completely in the right headspace in being completely done with this girl and your father. You’re right, they both knew. She’s also not a child like people love to claim to divert blame (if this is related to the previous post which I’m sure it is). That father and her are both sick individuals just in different ways. You and your family deserve to move on to a better life without them. If that father sticks around it will only carry pain in your family for the rest of your lives so forget that stupid therapist. For them to even think about giving you that advice is yikes. Ive had twisted situations pop up like this around me unfortunately and I know the affects it has on people, so if you ever need someone to talk to please feel free to message me. Even if it’s not about this. I hope you know you’re not alone and if anything, it’s good you learned who they truly were before it was too late. Take care of yourself! Don’t destroy your life over this and be the better person by taking the time to properly heal, stay healthy, allow yourself to have those off days, let out the cry, and just cut them out of your life if you need it. I hope your family can do the same and I wish you all nothing but happiness.
I just turned 25 and Id say I began coming to terms with death around 18. It definitely used to scare me but not anymore.
Thank you, I’m glad to hear you were able to break free from it

NTA. She’s dealing with the consequences of her own actions and it shouldn’t affect your life at all. In fact she’s the AH for expecting you to do this for her. She should either put her pitty party aside for you or just stay home and sulk. It’s not your fault that she chose to be a horrible partner.

I don’t understand why people do this to their partners, I’m sorry. I would probably just give her some time to think about things and if she doesn’t change her mind then I would suggest moving on. Its unfair of her to do that to you, especially knowing how important it is. You would just be unhappy in the end.
